Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

amorem 1.3.0

Changes in behaviour

  • rem() fits have class "amorem_rem" instead of "rem". The packages relevent and redeem register S3 methods on class "rem", so loading either of them re-pointed print(), summary(), coef(), plot(), predict() and logLik() for amorem fits. Code that tests inherits(fit, "rem") must test inherits(fit, "amorem_rem").

  • Tied times: statistics at time t use only events strictly before t, in every path of endogenous_features() (compiled and pure-R, with and without a history mask) and for event and control rows alike. Without a mask the compiled engine read ties in row order, so A->B and B->A at t = 1 gave reciprocity 0 1; they now give 0 0, as they already did with a mask.

  • endogenous_features() identifies the events of case-control data by the 0/1 event column whenever it is present, also when history_log or prior_log is given; history_log marks event rows by (sender, receiver, time) only for logs without an event column. Passing history_log = event_log no longer turns the controls of case-control data into events. A factor event column is read by its labels.

  • sample_non_events(scope = "citation") draws control receivers from every paper that has appeared in the log before the citing event, as a citing or a cited paper. Before, only papers that had already cited something were eligible, so papers that are only ever cited were never controls. The control sender is still the citing paper.

  • sample_non_events() orders the log by time before sampling (ties keep their input order); stratum k is the k-th event in that order. Appearance, removal and concurrency rules followed row order before, so an unsorted log gave controls drawn from actors and dyads of later events.

  • The no-control warning of sample_non_events() does not count events at the start of the log that come before the first event with a control, where the risk set is still being built; their strata are still listed in attr(, "no_control"). When no event has a control, all are counted. classroom_events with scope = "appearance", risk = "remove" gives no such warning; it counted events 2 and 3 before.

  • rem(method = "gam") warns when long input with more than one control per stratum is widened, since the gam design keeps the first control of each stratum, and points to method = "clogit", which uses every control. It only said that it widened the data.

  • rem() stops when re(x) has no x_ev / x_nv columns. With a single column x the term gives the event and its control the same level and is zero; the documented fallback to that column is removed.

  • simulate_relational_events(method = "gillespie") draws waiting times by thinning when a statistic changes between events (*_exp_decay, recency, *_time_*). It used to draw the waiting time from the rates at the previous event and choose the dyad from the undecayed state, so an reciprocity_exp_decay effect of 1.5 (half-life 0.5, 6 actors, 4000 events) was recovered as 2.22–2.69; it is now recovered as 1.37–1.61 (SE 0.12) over 10 replicates. Logs simulated with these statistics differ from those of earlier versions under the same seed. Logs without them are unchanged.

  • With a negative effect on recency or a *_time_* statistic the rates of simulate_relational_events() can decay toward zero; the simulation stops with a message once every rate is below exp(-700), and returns the events produced so far. It used to keep generating events.

  • transform_recency(half_life = T) gives weight 0.5 at a gap of T, exp(-delta * log(2) / T), the half-life convention of the *_exp_decay statistics. It used T as the e-folding scale (weight 0.368 at T). half_life = Inf gives weight 1 (no decay); it was an error. The median rule is unchanged.

  • compare_models(), compare_models_smooth() and compare_models_global() code time-since statistics as a recency weight plus an indicator (new argument recency = c("weight", "zero")). A time-since statistic (recency, every *_time_recent / *_time_first) is NA when there is no earlier event; the functions set it to 0, so “no earlier event” had the value of “an event a moment ago”. With recency = "weight" (the default) the statistic enters as w = transform_recency(delta) (median rule, w = 0 for no earlier event) plus the column <stat>_none = 1{no earlier event}. recency = "zero" is the old coding. On classroom_events with n_controls = 3, seed = 11 the AIC of the count / continuous / interrupted specifications is 1321.0 / 1842.3 / 1732.8 with "zero" and 1321.0 / 1124.5 / 1161.4 with "weight" (with random_effects = "sender": 1086.3 / 1581.4 / 1399.0 and 1086.3 / 905.0 / 812.4), so the ranking of count first came from the coding. Count, binary and exp-decay statistics are unaffected. n_terms counts the indicator columns.

  • simulate_relational_events() gives recency the value 0 for a dyad that has never fired, as for the *_time_* statistics and as endogenous_features() (NA) with NA -> 0. It used the time since start_time, so the rates of never-fired dyads grew with the clock under a recency effect and a model fitted with the post-hoc statistic was not the generating model: gof_univariate() rejected a correct linear recency model in 8.0% of replicates at the 5% level, against 4.5% with the simulator’s coding. Logs simulated with recency differ from those of earlier versions under the same seed.

New features

  • gof_univariate(), gof_multivariate(), gof_global() and gof_auxiliary() take n_samples (default 1). Each test is computed on one case-control sample, so its verdict depends on the seed: on classroom_events the univariate transitivity test rejects at 5% in 9 of 20 seeds. With n_samples = S > 1 the test runs on S control samples (seeds seed, seed + 1, …, or independent draws when seed is NULL) and the S p-values are combined with the Cauchy combination (Liu & Xie 2020), which is valid under arbitrary dependence among them. The result carries the combined p_value, the per-sample p_values and n_samples; the other fields come from the first sample. n_samples = 1 returns the same result as before for the same seed.

  • sample_non_events() takes entry: the time from which an actor can be a control sender, as a named numeric vector or a data.frame of actor and entry time; list(sender = , receiver = ) restricts both roles. Controls of the event at time t are drawn only from actors with entry time <= t, together with scope, risk, exclude_pairs and n_controls; events whose restricted risk set is empty are listed in attr(, "no_control"). attr(alien_mammals, "entry") can be passed as it is: with mode = "two", risk = "remove" and the never_at_risk exclusions, all 676 first records get a control, against 664 for drawing 10 unrestricted controls and keeping the first whose species had entered.

Bug fixes

  • gof_multivariate() holds its level. It referred sup_u ||W(u)||^2 to simulated q-dimensional Brownian bridges, with a ramp u C(1) for the effect of estimation, and its process came from a REML-penalised spline fit. The bridge is the limit only when the information of every spline column grows in proportion along the event sequence, which fails for a growing count, and the penalised fit selects its smoothing parameter from the same data. It rejected a correct linear model at the 5% level in 35.3% (reciprocity_count) and 17.5% (reciprocity_exp_decay) of replicates. The spline columns and the other covariates are now refitted without penalty (the model contains the linear null), and the p-value comes from a multiplier bootstrap that carries the estimation term A(u) V sum_i g_i (1 - pi_i) x_i (Lin, Wei & Ying 1993, as in gof_rem()). Over 1000 replicates of 1500 events (20 actors) the rejection rate at 5% is 4.8% (MC SE 0.7) for reciprocity_count, 4.7% (0.7) for reciprocity_exp_decay and 4.1% (0.6) for reciprocity_count next to transitivity_binary; with a step effect of reciprocity fitted as linear in the count it rejects in 6.5% (1.7) at 500 events and 66.5% (3.3) at 1500, against 1.5% and 43.0% before. n_sim is the number of bootstrap replicates; p-values differ from earlier versions for the same seed.

  • With n_samples > 1, a Monte Carlo p-value of 0 from gof_multivariate() or gof_auxiliary() enters the Cauchy combination as 1/(n_sim + 1) instead of 1e-15, so the combined p-value is at least 1/(n_sim + 1) (it was about 1e-15 whenever one sample had p = 0). p_values keeps the per-sample values. The Kolmogorov p-values of gof_univariate() and gof_global() are not floored.

  • The torch reproducibility test loads the amorem under test in its callr child process (the source tree under devtools::test(), the check library under R CMD check); it loaded the first amorem on the default library path, which can be another version.

  • print() and plot() of gof_rem() results report a bootstrap p-value of 0 as a bound, p < 1/n_sim (for example p < 0.001); they printed p = 0.000.

  • sample_non_events() warns when events get no control because their risk set holds no valid alternative (every other dyad excluded, removed or concurrent). Such events contribute nothing to the partial likelihood and were dropped without notice. Their strata are listed in attr(, "no_control"), also with shift = "exponential", where it equals attr(, "shift")$uninformative. Events before any actor has appeared under scope = "appearance" have no controls by construction and give no warning.

  • sample_non_events(risk = "remove") warns when a dyad fires more than once in the event log, which contradicts the one-event-per-dyad assumption of "remove".

  • The documentation of risk = "standard" says that dyads that have already fired stay at risk; it described them as “unrealized”. The documentation of rem(method = "nn") names the optional torch engine.

  • The pure-R path of endogenous_features() (taken when any statistic outside cpp_supported_stats() is requested, e.g. reciprocity_time_recent) reads a whole timestamp before adding its events to the history. It added each event before its same-time controls were computed, so a control saw its own event and the two engines disagreed on tied logs.

  • endogenous_features(history_log = ) no longer counts a control as an event when it coincides with another stratum’s event at the same time; such a control raised the outdegree and other statistics of later rows.

  • sample_non_events(scope = "appearance") admits only actors that appeared at an earlier timestamp; it admitted actors first seen in an earlier row with the same time. Under risk = "remove" a dyad likewise leaves the pool after the timestamp of its first event.

  • endogenous_features() and sample_non_events() stop with an error on NA times (also in history_log and prior_log). endogenous_features() hung on an NA time whenever a history mask was in use; the compiled loop now returns on non-finite times regardless.

  • sample_non_events() draws a valid control uniformly from the enumerated valid pairs after max_attempts rejection draws miss, as the shifted branch already did. It stopped with “Unable to sample a valid non-event” on runs where a valid control existed but was rare.

  • sample_non_events(shift = "exponential") accepts Date and POSIXct times and windows and returns times of the same class; it failed on them. A log with a single timestamp (default window) gives events without controls and a warning instead of an error. The shifted branch emits the same no-control warning as the ordinary branch.

  • sample_non_events() stops on a non-integer n_controls; 1.5 was truncated to 1. The documentation states that controls are drawn with replacement, so a stratum with a small risk set can hold the same control more than once.

  • standardize_event_log() reads a factor time column by its labels (it used the level codes, so "10" sorted before "2") and stops on text times that are not numbers, such as unconverted date strings (they became NA and, with drop_nas = TRUE, every row was dropped).

  • rem(), widen_case_control() and nn_uncertainty() read the event indicator by value: numeric or integer 0/1, logical, and character or factor "0"/"1" or "FALSE"/"TRUE". Any other value is an error. A factor column was read by its level codes (1 and 2), so method = "nn" trained on reversed labels, method = "clogit" without a stratum column built wrong strata, and widen_case_control() stopped with an error.

  • rem(method = "clogit") and rem(method = "nn") store the event-indicator column (fit$case) and the stratum argument, and nn_uncertainty() uses them. It took the first variable of the formula as the event indicator, so rem(~ x + y, case = "event") was bootstrapped with x as the indicator.

  • compare_models_global() evaluates a global covariate at time t with the value of the last grid time at or before t. A time at or after the last grid time took the second-to-last value. A time before the first grid time takes the first value, as before; the documentation says so.

  • rem() uses offset() terms; they were dropped without notice. For method = "clogit" the offset expression is evaluated on the rows of data and the fit equals survival::clogit() with the same offset. For method = "gam", offset(o) names a column resolved like a linear term (an event-minus-control difference: o, else d_o, else o_ev - o_nv). method = "nn" stops when the formula has an offset.

  • rem(method = "clogit") reports in fit$n the rows the fit used and records them in fit$rows, with a warning when rows with missing values are left out, as method = "gam" does. fit$n counted every row of data.

  • predict() on a rem(method = "gam") fit takes wide data in the form rem() accepts and builds the internal design columns from it. It needed the internal column names in newdata.

  • A rem(method = "nn") fit with nn_control(engine = "torch") and a seed gives the same result on the first fit of a session as on later ones: torch is loaded before the seed is set, since loading it draws from the random-number generator. nn_uncertainty() does the same before seeding its resampling.

  • simulate_relational_events() and simulate_directed_hyperevents_tvnl() draw valid controls when one candidate is left. sample(x, n) on a length-1 pool drew from 1:x, so with two actors and n_controls = 1 controls were loops or equal to their case.

  • simulate_relational_events(), simulate_hyperedge_events(), simulate_directed_hyperedge_events() and simulate_directed_hyperevents_tvnl() compute selection weights as exp(log_w - max(log_w)) and keep the total rate on its scale for waiting times. A log-intensity above 709 overflowed and the dyad was set to rate 0; a very small one underflowed to 0 and the dyad left the control pool. A log-intensity of NaN or +Inf is an error. Under method = "tau_leap", and in simulate_directed_hyperevents_tvnl(), rates too large to simulate stop with a message.

  • simulate_relational_events(method = "tau_leap") records the cyclic_*, sending_balance_* and receiving_balance_* *_time_*_ordered statistics at each event’s time, as it does for transitivity; they were recorded at the start of the step.

  • simulate_relational_events(risk = "remove", n_controls > 0) stops with a message when fewer than n_controls + 1 dyads remain in the risk set and returns the events produced so far; it stopped with an error.

  • simulate_relational_events(n_events = 0, n_controls > 0) returns the columns in the order of a non-empty result (stratum, event first).

  • simulate_relational_events() stops when n_events or n_controls is not a whole number, and simulate_hyperedge_events(), simulate_directed_hyperedge_events() and simulate_directed_hyperevents_tvnl() do the same for n_events and n_controls; non-integer values were truncated.

  • simulate_directed_hyperevents_tvnl() cuts its last grid cell at horizon; events could fall past it (1.0048 with horizon = 1). Its documentation describes the piecewise-constant midpoint scheme it uses; it called it thinning.

  • simulate_hyperedge_events() and simulate_directed_hyperedge_events() reject subrep_0 and subrep_0_<l>, which hyperedge_features() rejects.

  • hyperedge_log() rejects an actor listed twice in one event’s I or J, and NA or empty actor names.

Documentation

  • gof_multivariate(), gof_global(), gof_auxiliary(), nn_control() and nn_uncertainty() have runnable examples. The rem() and gof_rem() examples run only when mgcv is installed.

  • The rem() return value lists rows, case, stratum and the predict() method.

  • alien_invasions has 259 regions (the help page said 272); start equals stop in 421 rows, 407 of them after 1880 (the page said only in 1880).

  • classroom_events$weight is numeric, 1 for direct and 0.2 for broadcast communication; social_evolution_actors$gradeType has levels "1"–"5"; social_evolution_calls spans 6 September to 18 October 2008.

  • The help pages of classroom_*, social_evolution_*, college_msg and email_eu_core state the licence situation of their sources: no licence is stated for any of these data; networkDynamic and goldfish, which distribute two of them, are GPL. The Social Evolution page records the MIT Reality Commons request not to redistribute the data.

amorem 1.2.0

CRAN release: 2026-10-18

Bug fixes

  • rem(method = "gam") warns when rows with missing covariate values are left out of the fit, and records which rows it used (fit$rows, with fit$n counting only those). gof_rem() keeps the same rows when given the full data; it stopped with “non-conformable arguments” before.

  • sample_non_events(scope = "citation") always draws the citing paper and the cited papers from separate pools. Under the mode = "one" default of 1.1.0 it pooled them, so most controls had a sender other than the citing paper.

  • rem(method = "nn") and nn_uncertainty() no longer change the caller’s random-number state when given a seed (CRAN policy); fitted results are unchanged.

  • Partial-dependence curves of plot() on neural fits and of nn_uncertainty() span the 1st to 99th percentile of each feature instead of the mean ± 2 standard deviations, which reached below the data for skewed, non-negative statistics.

  • Concordance of neural fits splits a tied top score evenly between the tied candidates; it gave the whole stratum to the event.

  • simulate_relational_events(method = "tau_leap") stops with a message when a single step would draw more than ten million events, which happens when an effect grows without bound; it could exhaust memory.

New features

  • gof_rem() tests a model fitted with rem(method = "gam") with cumulative martingale residuals (Boschi & Wit 2025): over event time (test = "time"), over the quantiles of a covariate (test = "functional_form", which detects a wrong shape of the effect), or over the quantiles weighted by the term’s basis (test = "functional_form_score"). It works on linear and smooth terms of the fitted model, and its null distribution is a multiplier bootstrap that subtracts the drift from estimating the coefficients. It has print() and plot() methods (plot() takes main and a legend position). The existing gof_univariate(), gof_multivariate(), gof_global() and gof_auxiliary() are unchanged.

  • rem() fits store the name of their time column.

Datasets

  • New alien_mammals: the risk table of the first records of alien mammals with the covariates of Juozaitienė et al. (2023) (distance to the nearest invaded region, trade, temperature difference, colonial ties, land use), and the never-at-risk pairs and species entry years as attributes; used in the species-invasion section of the software paper.

  • New event logs, all under licences that allow redistribution: copenhagen_calls, copenhagen_sms and copenhagen_actors (Copenhagen Networks Study, MIT); us_leader_visits (leader-to-leader visits to and from the United States, 1945-2019, CC0); football_results (men’s international football matches since 1872, CC0); ucdp_dyads (UCDP armed-conflict dyads, 1946-2025, CC BY 4.0); alien_invasions (first records of alien species by region, 1880-2005, CC0).

  • New hyperevent log: congress_bills_118, one sponsor and the cosponsors of each bill of the 118th US Congress, with congress_members_118 (public domain).

  • New global covariates: oni (Oceanic Nino Index since 1950), daily_weather (NOAA daily temperature and precipitation for the cities of the bundled email and messaging logs) and public_holidays.

  • radoslaw_email is rebuilt from the authors’ CC0 release (Nurek & Michalski 2020, doi:10.7910/DVN/6Z3CGX). It keeps the original employee ids, which match the new radoslaw_hierarchy (who reports to whom), and its timestamps are read as Warsaw local time. The previous copy, from Network Repository, read them as UTC, so it ignored daylight saving time: events sent during Polish summer time are now one hour earlier relative to the first event, and unix_origin is one hour earlier. The number of events and each employee’s activity are unchanged.

  • The pkgdown site has a data catalogue: licences, download code and structural profiles of 78 relational-event datasets and covariates, including the many whose licences do not allow amorem to redistribute them.

amorem 1.1.0

CRAN release: 2026-10-17

Bug fixes

  • Endogenous statistics on case-control data no longer count the sampled controls as events. endogenous_features() on the output of sample_non_events() (a 0/1 event column with control rows) now builds the network history from the event == 1 rows only; the controls read it but never enter it. Before, every row updated the history, so each statistic also counted hypothetical dyads. This was the default path inside compare_models(), compare_models_smooth(), gof(), martingale_residuals() and the vignettes. On six simulated datasets with a reciprocity effect of 0.3, the estimate moved from 0.20 to 0.31 on average. Results of those functions change and should be re-run. Pass history_log = event_log to treat every row as an event.

  • rem() evaluates tv() and tvnl() terms at each row’s own time. When data has time_ev / time_nv instead of a single time column (the wide form of sample_non_events(shift = "exponential")), tv(x) contributes beta(t) x_ev - beta(t*) x_nv and tvnl() uses both times. Before, the event time was used for both rows. Models with a single time column give the same formula and fit as before.

  • compare_models_global() now uses the paper’s time-shifted design. It drew one shift per control row, never shifted the event, never checked the observation window (control times could precede the data), evaluated the controls’ dyadic statistics at the event time, and let sampled controls enter the network history. On simulated data with a global effect of 1 it returned estimates of -1.74, 2.63 and -2.12 over three datasets. It now draws its sample with sample_non_events(shift = "exponential"), computes dyadic statistics against the real history at each row’s own time, evaluates tv / tvnl terms at each row’s own time, and drops events with no control; the same three datasets give 0.85, 1.02 and 1.01. The shift mean is now shift_scale times the average event time (it was times the average inter-arrival time), and a window argument is passed through. Results of earlier compare_models_global() fits change and should be re-run.

  • widen_case_control() and the clogit / nn backends of rem() use the stratum column written by sample_non_events() when stratum = NULL, instead of rebuilding strata as cumsum(case == 1). The rebuilt strata assumed each case was followed by its controls, which stops holding once endogenous_features() re-sorts rows by time with ties, or with shifted controls, and then paired cases with the wrong controls. Data without a stratum column (eventnet output) is handled as before.

  • sample_non_events() risk-set edge cases (#102).

    • exclude_pairs and, under risk = "remove", same-time events are now part of the check for whether any valid control exists, so a stratum whose every alternative is excluded gets no controls instead of stopping with “Unable to sample a valid non-event after max_attempts attempts”.
    • scope = "appearance" no longer falls back to all actors when no actor has appeared yet: the first event gets no controls, and controls are only ever drawn from actors seen in prior events, as documented. Results change for the first stratum(s) of scope = "appearance" fits.
    • Factor sender / receiver columns are coerced to character, so the output columns are character whatever the input type.
    • The documentation of mode states which risk set each mode gives: "two" never draws a receiver-only actor as a control sender (or vice versa), so networks with one node set should use mode = "one".
    • The unreachable empty-pool fallbacks in the pair sampler were removed.

Changes in behaviour

  • sample_non_events() now defaults to mode = "one", the risk set of networks whose senders and receivers are one node set, and the default of compare_models(), compare_models_smooth(), compare_models_global(), gof() and martingale_residuals(). Calls that relied on the old default mode = "two" (bipartite networks) must now pass it.

New features

  • New dataset enso_nino34: the tree-ring reconstruction of the November–January Niño3.4 sea-surface temperature anomaly by Li et al. (2013), one value per year from 1301 to 2005 (NOAA NCEI study 14632), as a global covariate on a yearly clock. The raw NOAA file ships in inst/extdata/enso_nino34/, and data-raw/enso_nino34.R rebuilds the object.

  • vignette("species-invasion") now simulates five centuries of invasions (1500–2005) driven by distance, a neighbour pressure and ENSO. It shows that ordinary case-control sampling gives an ENSO difference of zero in every stratum, and recovers all three effects with time-shifted sampling and rem(), reporting standard errors.

  • Time-shifted case-control sampling for global covariates (#101). sample_non_events(shift = "exponential") implements Section 4 of Lembo, Juozaitienė, Vinciotti & Wit (2025, JRSS-C): one exponential shift per dyad, each control drawn uniformly from the dyads whose back-shifted time lies in the observation window and stored at that time, so covariates that depend only on time no longer cancel within strata. shift_scale sets the mean shift as a multiple of the average event time, as in the paper. Risk-set rules (exclude_pairs, risk = "remove", scope = "appearance") are evaluated at the control’s own time; events with no other dyad in their shifted risk set get no control and are listed in attr(, "shift")$uninformative. The attribute also holds the shift mean, the window and the per-dyad shifts.

  • endogenous_features(history_log = ) and prior_log now work for every statistic, including reciprocity_exp_decay, reciprocity_time_recent and reciprocity_time_first, which the compiled engine does not cover.

  • Per-term basis settings in rem() formulas (#91). Smooth terms take the basis arguments of mgcv::s() / mgcv::te() after the covariate, so terms in one model can use different basis dimensions and types: tv(x, k = 20, bs = "cr") + nl(y, k = 5, bs = "ps"). tvnl() takes one value per margin (tvnl(x, k = c(5, 8))). A new global bs argument joins the global k as the default for terms that set neither; existing formulas give the same model as before.

  • sample_non_events(exclude_concurrent = ) controls whether dyads with an event at the focal event’s own time can be controls. The default keeps the existing behaviour: excluded under risk = "remove", at risk under risk = "standard" (the Breslow convention).

amorem 1.0.1

Bug fixes

  • compare_models() did not stratify on the matched sets under survival before 3.7-3. The Cox formula was built with a namespace-qualified survival::strata(stratum), and terms(specials = ) does not match a qualified call, so the matched-set identifier was silently fitted as an ordinary factor covariate in an unstratified model. Coefficients and the delta_AIC column were unaffected; the absolute log_lik was shifted by -n_events * log(n_strata) and the degrees of freedom inflated by n_strata - 1, so reported AIC values were wrong. The same applied to the frailty() terms on the random-effects path, which is why the coxme two-axis fit did not complete. All four call sites now use bare specials, which every survival version matches, and regression tests assert that AIC == -2 * log_lik + 2 * df and that no stratum dummies enter as covariates. Anyone who published absolute log-likelihood or AIC values from compare_models(n_controls > 1) should re-run them.

amorem 1.0.0

CRAN release: 2026-06-29

First CRAN release, under the name amorem. The package was renamed from the working name amore, which collided (case-insensitively) with the archived CRAN package AMORE. This release consolidates the 0.9.0 development line into the first stable, installable version: the unified rem() front-end (the clogit, gam, and nn backends, including the additive-spline architecture), the Gillespie / tau-leap simulation engine, the endogenous-statistics catalogue, and the martingale-residual goodness-of-fit family. Relative to 0.9.0 the package was renamed to amorem and the exported feature functions dropped their compute_ prefix — compute_endogenous_features() and compute_hyperedge_features() became endogenous_features() and hyperedge_features(); the rest of the API is unchanged.

New features

  • torch training engine for rem(method = "nn"). nn_control(engine = "torch") trains the same model and conditional-logistic loss as the built-in pure-R engine using torch (libtorch autograd + Adam), markedly faster and, with batch_strata, scaling to large event logs (optionally on GPU). The fitted object is interchangeable with the R engine. torch is a Suggests dependency; the torch engine requires equal-sized strata.
  • nn_uncertainty() quantifies uncertainty for a neural fit by a stratum bootstrap, returning partial-dependence uncertainty bands and a concordance confidence interval (with print() and plot() methods) — the inferential counterpart the point-prediction nn backend otherwise lacks.

amorem 0.9.0

New neural backend and a small number of API refinements; the version intended for the first CRAN release.

  • STREAM-style additive splines: nn_control(architecture = "additive_spline", batch_strata = ) fits per-covariate B-spline effects by (mini-batch) stochastic gradient on the exact case-control partial likelihood — the construction of Filippi-Mazzola & Wit (2024, JRSS-C, doi:10.1093/jrsssc/qlae023) — giving interpretable additive smooth curves on the same objective as clogit, with mini-batching for large event logs.
  • New rem(method = "nn") backend: a multilayer perceptron scores every candidate in a case-control stratum and is trained on the conditional-logistic partial likelihood (softmax over each risk set) — a nonlinear, prediction-oriented counterpart of clogit. Pure-R implementation (no extra dependencies), configured via nn_control(); summary() reports in-sample (and, with a validation split, held-out) concordance and plot(type = "pdp") shows per-feature partial-dependence curves.
  • API: the degenerate-logistic backend is now method = "gam" (was "degenerate"); the smooth-term wrappers are tv() / nl() / tvnl() (was tve() / nle() / tvnle()); re() is unchanged.
  • rem()’s case argument now defaults to NULL and is taken from the formula’s left-hand side (e.g. event ~ x) for the clogit/nn backends.
  • widen_case_control() auto-detects the 0/1 indicator column (event or IS_OBSERVED) when case is not given.
  • widen_case_control() now carries the sender/receiver identifiers of the case and its matched control into the output (sender_ev/receiver_ev/ sender_nv/receiver_nv); the new keep_ids argument controls this (default TRUE). The dyads behind each pair are no longer lost, and re() grouping terms can reach the actor levels (#92).
  • rem(method = "gam") now detects long-format case-control input (a event/IS_OBSERVED indicator with control rows) and widens it with widen_case_control() before fitting, emitting a message — instead of silently misreading raw per-row values as event-minus-control differences (#93).
  • compute_endogenous_features() gains a prior_log argument for warm-starting the network state from events that precede the study window: its rows update the running state but never appear in the output, separating warm-starting from the non-event masking role of history_log (#94).
  • cpp_supported_stats() is now exported.

amorem 0.1.0

First release.

  • rem() unified fitter for preprocessed case-control data, with a gam (case-1-control logistic via mgcv::gam()) and a clogit backend.
  • Smooth-term formula wrappers for the gam backend (time-varying, non-linear, time-varying-non-linear) and an re() grouping random effect; re() reproduces the Intro-to-REM tutorial parameterization, and rem() exposes a gam_method argument.
  • Simulation via simulate_relational_events() (Gillespie and tau-leap), the endogenous-statistic feature engine, non-event sampling, and the martingale-residual goodness-of-fit family.
